name: Jakarta Running Festival 2026
short_description: Jakarta Running Festival 2026 is a full marathon, half marathon, 10km and 5km event at Gelora Bung Karno in Jakarta, Indonesia, with the half marathon on 24 October and the marathon on 25 October 2026.
ai_summary: Jakarta Running Festival 2026 is a multi-distance road race based at the Gelora Bung Karno (GBK) Sports Complex in Jakarta, Indonesia. The half marathon starts at 4.30am on Saturday 24 October 2026 and the marathon at 4am on Sunday 25 October 2026. Runners can choose between a full marathon (42.195km), half marathon (21.1km), 10km or 5km. In 2025 the marathon and half marathon held World Athletics Label status.

core_facts.venue: Gelora Bung Karno (GBK) Sports Complex, Senayan

pros: Flat city loop: the marathon stays between about 10 m and 30 m elevation
Roads on the course closed from 3am on marathon day, and the Sunday car-free day is cancelled for it
Water every 1.5 to 2.5 km, with a medical station at every hydration point
Free MRT for runners and trains from 3am to the GBK start
Half-marathon limit raised to 3 hours 45 minutes for 2026
cons: Strict five-hour marathon limit with four time-of-day checkpoints, the first at km 15
Near-saturated air: 25°C and 100% humidity at the 2025 marathon start
Very large field (27,300 in 2025), so the shorter races are crowded
Race packs must be collected at the expo before race day; no race-day pickup

excerpt_quotes.quote: Despite the heat and the sweat, I crossed the line in 3 hours 38 minutes, placing 13th in the open category.
excerpt_quotes.attribution: Josh Fothergill, race report on TaSH Harriers club site

excerpt_quotes.quote: Not my fastest marathon by any means—an hour slower than London earlier this year—but definitely one of the most memorable.
excerpt_quotes.attribution: Josh Fothergill, race report on TaSH Harriers club site

excerpt_quotes.quote: I was hoping for a PB, but the conditions were tough, and I decided to hold back a little to save something for the next day.
excerpt_quotes.attribution: Josh Fothergill, on running the half marathon day one of JRF 2025, TaSH Harriers club site

excerpt_quotes.quote: The final stretch was packed with cheering crowds, laughter, and support
excerpt_quotes.attribution: Josh Fothergill, race report on TaSH Harriers club site

research_highlights: The event runs across two dedicated race days: half marathon and 5K on the Saturday, with the marathon and 10K on the Sunday (or vice versa depending on the year), so runners doing multiple distances back-to-back is possible — one 2025 participant ran the half on Saturday and the full marathon on Sunday, covering 63km over the weekend per the runner's own account on tasharriers.club.
Marathon cut-off is a strict 5 hours, deliberately shorter than many other marathons, specifically because of Jakarta's heat and humidity, according to the official event site.
At the 4am start of the 2025 marathon (26 October) Halim Perdanakusuma airport recorded 25°C and 100% humidity; by 9.30am it was 32°C.

The course starts/finishes around the Gelora Bung Karno (GBK) Sports Complex and passes Jakarta landmarks such as Monas, with early start times built in to help runners beat the heat, per the race's own description on Ahotu.
Race is a World Athletics Label event with elite fields alongside mass participation, plus an expo, cheer zones and live music as part of the festival format.
research_watchouts: Runners consistently describe conditions as hot and humid, with one participant explicitly noting they finished 'despite the heat and the sweat' and about an hour slower than a cooler European race the same year.
The half marathon on the Saturday was also described as tough conditions-wise by a participant who deliberately held back pace rather than chase a PB.
The organizers themselves warn the marathon cut-off (5 hours) is stricter/shorter than comparable races, meaning slower runners need to be confident of finishing within that window.
Air quality in Jakarta is flagged as something participants should monitor during their visit, per race directory notes.

faqs.question: When does the Jakarta Running Festival 2026 take place?
faqs.answer: The Jakarta Running Festival 2026 has two race days at the Gelora Bung Karno Sports Complex. The half marathon starts at 4.30am on Saturday 24 October 2026 and the marathon at 4.00am on Sunday 25 October 2026, according to the official event pages. In 2025 the 5K ran with the half and the 10K with the marathon.

faqs.question: What race distances are available at this event?
faqs.answer: The Jakarta Running Festival 2026 offers four distance options for participants: a full marathon of 42.195km, a half marathon of 21.1km, a 10km race, and a 5km race. This range allows both competitive marathoners and casual runners to take part.

faqs.question: Where exactly in Jakarta is the race held?
faqs.answer: The race is based at the Gelora Bung Karno (GBK) Sports Complex in Senayan, central Jakarta, where the marathon and half marathon start and finish. In 2025 the marathon course looped through Sudirman, Thamrin, Monas and Rasuna Said, and runners had free MRT rides to Istora Mandiri station, a six-minute walk from the venue.
